PAY APPLICATION GENERATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Work out this month's pay application, retainage included.

Paste your schedule of values with what was billed before and what you are billing now. The page returns the contract sum, change orders, retainage held, previous certificates and the payment due, a line-by-line table, and flags any line that is billed over its value before the owner's reviewer finds it.

The numbers are read in this browser tab and never leave your device. It does the arithmetic from what you enter; your contract decides the retainage terms. It is not the AIA G702/G703 form and is not affiliated with the AIA.

1. Your schedule of values

A CSV or a range pasted from a spreadsheet, with a header row. Required: description and scheduled value. Then: previous (billed in earlier applications), this period, stored (materials presently stored). Put CO in the item column for change orders; a deductive change order is a negative value. Optional: a retainage column for a line with its own rate.

2. Retainage and the application

Choose a file or paste the schedule, then click Work out the application.

What it does, and what it leaves to you

    
    
      
  • Per line: completed and stored = previous + this period + stored; percent complete; balance to finish; retainage = work rate on previous and this period plus stored rate on stored materials, rounded to the cent.
    • 
      
  • Summary: original contract sum, net change orders, contract sum to date, total completed and stored, retainage, total earned less retainage, less previous certificates, current payment due, balance to finish including retainage.
    • 
      
  • Findings: a line billed over its value, work on a line with no value, a negative payment due, a front-loading pattern, and an estimated previous-certificates figure.
    • 
      
  • Not decided: what your contract allows for retainage, stored-material billing, and reduction; state limits on retainage, prompt-payment and lien rules; whether a change order is approved; sales tax; and whether the owner will certify the amount.
    • 
    

  


  

    
Common questions

    
What is a pay application?

    
A pay application (also called a payment application, progress billing or draw request) is the document a contractor sends the owner each period to be paid for the work done so far. It shows the contract sum, change orders, how much is complete and stored, the retainage held back, what was already paid, and what is due now.

    
How is retainage calculated on a pay application?

    
Retainage is a percentage of the work completed and stored to date, commonly 5 to 10 percent. This page multiplies each line's completed work by the work rate and its stored materials by the stored rate, rounds to the cent per line, and adds them. It can also drop the rate once the job passes a completion point, if your contract allows it.

    
How do I fill in the previous certificates line?

    
Take it from your last application: the current payment due that was certified, summed across all earlier applications. If you leave it blank this page estimates it as previous work less retainage at today's rate, and says so in the findings, because that only holds if the rate never changed.

    
How do change orders work?

    
Add each approved change order as its own line with a negative or positive scheduled value, and put CO in the item column (CO-1, CO-2) or in a Type column. They are separated from the original contract sum and shown as the net change.

    
Is this the AIA G702 and G703 form?

    
No. It produces the same kind of summary and line-by-line table, in plain text and CSV, but it is not the AIA form, which is copyrighted, and it is not affiliated with the American Institute of Architects. If your owner requires the AIA form, use the numbers here to fill it in.

    
Is my project data uploaded anywhere?

    
No. The schedule is read in your browser and nothing is sent; a test in the code asserts there are no network calls.

  


  

    
No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, accounting, compliance, or financial advice, and it does not replace your contract, your accountant, or an attorney. A summary it writes is a worksheet for you to check before you send it.

    
Not affiliated with the American Institute of Architects. AIA, G702 and G703 are the property of their owner. This tool is independent and produces its own plain-text summary and CSV; it does not reproduce the AIA form.

    
Project data. A schedule of values can be commercially sensitive. This page runs in your browser and sends nothing anywhere, and the portfolio never receives it. Closing the tab discards it; downloads are files on your own device.

    
Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record: nothing you enter is saved anywhere.

    
Everything runs in your browser. Your schedule is never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (schedule_calculated, example_loaded, summary_downloaded, csv_downloaded) are counted only in local storage on your device, never with any of your data, and are switched off by Do Not Track.

    

    
Related tools: the contractor WIP schedule and the mechanics lien deadline calculator sit on either side of a pay application. The lien waiver checker reads the waiver that comes back with the payment.

    
Free and open source. If this helped, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.
